source.title: Following the crowd: brain substrates of long-term memory conformity

confidence_rationale: Shows that socially induced memory errors come in two kinds, temporary (public compliance, reversed when the social source is revealed as unreliable) and long-lasting (the internal memory itself rewritten), with a separate neural signature (enhanced amygdala activity and amygdala-hippocampal coupling) predicting only the long-lasting kind. So social agreement can stay in a separable, retractable channel OR cross into internal representation, and the crossing is neurally marked. That is ARC-115's distinction and its failure mode. Discounted for mapping: memory, not confidence readouts.
failure_signatures: Participants conformed to erroneous group recollections even when their initial memory was strong and accurate, showing socially supplied content can overwrite internally derived content.

The dissociation is between two outcomes (transient vs persistent error), not between two concurrently live readout channels, so it bears on ARC-115's cost claim more directly than on its channel architecture.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Participants conformed to erroneous recollections of a group, producing both temporary and long-lasting memory errors even when their original memory was strong and accurate; enhanced amygdala activity and amygdala-hippocampus connectivity predicted the long-lasting but not the temporary alterations.
mapping.ree_translation: Temporary conformity is social agreement held in a separate, retractable channel (it disappears once the source is discredited); persistent conformity is social agreement that has entered the internal store and lost its provenance. ARC-115 says an agent must be built so that the first stays the norm. The paper shows both routes exist in humans and that the crossing has a distinct neural signature: a biological precedent for keeping the channels distinguishable.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Episodic memory for a film, not confidence readouts or commit-readiness. The amygdala finding points to an affective gate on when social content is internalised, which links to MECH-192 (z_beta leakage) more than to propositional confidence. Separate channels are inferred from separable outcomes, not observed as parallel readouts.
mapping.source_context: Healthy adults watched a documentary, then answered memory questions after seeing manipulated answers from co-viewers; fMRI during the social manipulation; retest after the manipulation was revealed.

confidence_components.notes: Science, strong design with a reveal-and-retest dissociation. Mapping moderate-low (memory not confidence), which keeps confidence near 0.55.
